- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.7) and model forecast is trending upward, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.  
- If recent true outcomes show sharp downward spikes after high peaks, model should adjust downward with lagged momentum correction.  
- When official event net supply is negative and bullish sentiment is high, model should not ignore policy-driven mean reversion — forecast should slightly undershoot peak expectations.  
- If model forecast is flat or rising slowly but true outcome shows rapid decline, apply downward bias correction starting from 3rd day of forecast horizon.  
- For multi-day forecasts with high event count and negative supply net, apply “event decay” heuristic: reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per event beyond 10 events.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model should avoid linear extrapolation — use smoothing filter with 3-day moving average for trend correction.  
- When supply net is negative and bullish sentiment is low, model should not assume continuation — forecast should reflect bearish bias with 1–2% downward adjustment.
